heuristic.applicability: Prefer when the drawer is open, red is on or being released over its pad, blue is observed outside the drawer, and blue is displaced or rotated relative to the narrow demonstrated pickup region. The source_object argument must be blue and destination_field must be blue_goal. It remains applicable through nominal insertion, but its special advantage is source acquisition and early transport.

handoff.entry_conditions: drawer_position is strictly above 0.26 m; red is still held/touching down at the outside pad or has just been released; blue is observed outside and is the intended object; the requested source is blue and destination is blue_goal.
handoff.exit_conditions: Use the unchanged evaluator condition: drawer open, red fully on its outside pad at the required z, and blue fully inside the drawer cavity at the required z in one observation. Observed open fingers and high retreat are transition context, not extra success requirements.
handoff.failure_signatures: IK non-convergence/limit contacts; blue/TCP fail to co-move after closure; block pose changes within the chunk; TCP approaches red rather than blue; red leaves its pad; block approaches drawer wall/lip; or blue remains outside cavity/z bounds.
handoff.overlap_role: Preserves every action in [600,stop) and therefore the full [600,850) overlap with red_transfer: final red lowering/release, retreat, cross-scene transit, blue approach, close and lift. The blue-frame mechanism only changes action coordinates, not labels or cut coverage.
handoff.successor_readiness: There is no learned successor. On nominal completion, hand control to framework evaluation. If blue is held and near the drawer but destination alignment is uncertain, the destination-frame prior is the preferred continuation before declaring completion.

heuristic.limitations: Object-relative output does not make reachability invariant: a displaced blue block can be unreachable or can require a collision-free route absent from demonstrations. Freezing the source frame for an eight-action chunk assumes the observed pose is sufficiently reliable; if the block slips after sampling, targets do not automatically re-anchor until replanning. During final insertion, source anchoring can be less stable than destination anchoring. Demonstrations contain no failed grasps, drops, wall impacts or recovery, and object/TCP proximity is not contact truth.
heuristic.pipeline_implications: At each replan, build_inputs resolves the current blue pose and freezes it as chunk_context. encode_targets expresses all 16 demonstrated commanded TCP poses in that same causal frame as 3-D position plus 6-D rotation and gripper scalar. decode_action reconstructs a world pose from the frozen blue frame and calls the supplied IK from freshly measured joints. Inputs use two causal frames and fixed physical scaling; no label augmentation or backbone change is used. The high-level agent should switch to the destination-frame prior if drawer alignment dominates source displacement.
heuristic.rationale: Observed support is narrow for the source pose: across the twelve segment starts blue x is about -0.414 to -0.387 m and y is about 0.287 to 0.315 m. In demo1000 the free blue remains near (-0.401,0.291) through the approach, the TCP descends over it by 800, closure occurs by 820, and TCP/blue co-motion is visible during lift at 840-850. The expected benefit, not demonstrated recovery, is exact equivariance of decoded Cartesian targets to a changed observed blue pose over pickup, closure, lift and early carry. Robot qpos/qvel, world blue pose, drawer state, destination offset and red-pad residual remain inputs so reachability and task dependencies are not discarded.
heuristic.statement: Blue-frame equivariant Cartesian targets for source displacement. Learn each commanded TCP target as a pose in the causal chunk-start blue-block frame, with object-relative TCP/destination features plus world blue pose and robot state. This construction translates and rotates pickup, grasp and lift targets with an observed displaced blue block, while destination-relative conditioning still permits transport toward the drawer.

subgoal: Primary responsibility: finish the predecessor red release/retreat context, acquire the blue block outside the drawer, lift and transport it to the open drawer cavity, lower it inside, release it, and retreat to a high clear pose. The intended object is blue; the red block visible at segment entry is only the predecessor object still being lowered/released. Observed contact/motion: at observation 600 red is still pinched near the pad at z about 0.032-0.037 m; by 700 red is settled at z about 0.020 m and the open gripper is retreating toward blue; around 800 the TCP descends over blue; by 850 blue is pinched and lifted; later it is carried to the drawer, lowered to z about 0.063 m, released, and the TCP retreats to z about 0.323 m. Final observations in all occurrences simultaneously show drawer_position about 0.297, red near (-0.176 to -0.177,-0.298 to -0.304,0.020), and blue near (-0.171 to -0.173,0.073 to 0.074,0.063), satisfying the supplied one-observation completion rule. The demo1000 final front image supports blue in the drawer, red on the outside pad, and the open drawer. Purpose/expected benefit: retaining the long release-to-pick overlap should make this independently trained insertion model usable from intermediate transition states; demonstrated success does not establish recovery from dropped blue blocks, drawer collisions, or unseen placements.
